chunks: And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, so it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said, 'I will surely kill you.' He said, 'Allah only accepts from the God-conscious.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the two sons of Adam in the Quran and what does it teach about acceptance by God?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in Surah Al-Ma'idah, establishes the foundational Shia principle that divine acceptance (qabul) is contingent upon taqwa (God-consciousness) rather than ritual form alone, as demonstrated by Habil's humble offering versus Qabil's arrogant one. It serves as a critical exegetical link to the concept of 'Ahl al-Bayt' and the Imams, who embody perfect taqwa, contrasting with those who reject divine guidance despite outward piety. The narrative underscores the inevitability of conflict between the righteous and the arrogant, a theme central to Shia historical consciousness.
